correctness.rationale: For precisely two compact convex pieces with disjoint interiors and union a square, convex separation forces their common interface to be a straight cut. Equal area in a centrally symmetric square forces the line through center; square symmetries reduce y=tx,0≤t≤1. For trapezoid K_t=conv{(−1,−t),(−1,1),(1,1),(1,t)}, supporting-line constraints give sharp inradius r=(1+t)/(1+t+√(1+t²)) attained by a specified center. An enclosing circle with the diameter from (−1,−t) to (1,1) contains the other corners, giving R=√(4+(1+t)²)/2. The exact log derivative of f=r/R has sign of H(t)=4(1−t)−(t+√(1+t²))(1+t)³; H strictly decreases from +3 to negative, giving unique t*=0.28867838972... and optimum 0.465023362935585... up to symmetries. Independent symbolic differentiation and exact polynomial squaring checks plus root bracket and endpoint comparisons completed.
